{{Quote|Darth Plagueis was a Dark Lord of the Sith, so powerful and so wise, he could use the Force to influence the midi-chlorians to create life. He had such a knowledge of the dark side, he could even keep the ones he cared about from dying.|Sheev Palpatine to Anakin Skywalker|<ref name="ROTS" />}}
'''Darth Plagueis''' {{Pronounced|'pleɪɡ.əs}} was a [[Muun]] [[Dark Lord of the Sith]] who secretly trained "[[the Stranger]]" and [[Darth Sidious]] in the ways of the [[Sith]] as his [[Sith apprentice|apprentices]]. Plagueis lusted for [[immortality]], believing the secret lay in [[science]]. To that end, he researched [[bioengineering]] with Sidious, who possessed a strong connection to [[the Force]], and experimented with his ability to influence the [[midi-chlorian]]s to create life. In doing so, Plagueis acquired considerable knowledge of the Force, but was ultimately betrayed and [[Death|murdered]] by his own apprentice in accordance with the [[Rule of Two]], which limited the [[Sith Lord]]s' ranks to one [[Sith Master|master]] and one apprentice. Sidious later recounted the "[[Tragedy of Darth Plagueis the Wise|legend]]" of his master's demise to lure the [[Jedi Knight]] [[Anakin Skywalker]] to the [[dark side of the Force]], calling the fallen Sith Lord '''Darth Plagueis the Wise'''. After his own [[Battle of Endor|demise]], Sidious used his master's teachings to [[Transference|cheat death]], but he was [[Battle of Exegol|permanently destroyed]] by his granddaughter, [[Rey Skywalker|Rey]].

==Biography==
===Dweller in the Dark===
[[File:Acolyte-Thereheis.png|thumb|right|350px|The mysterious Darth Plagueis (pictured in shadow) rose to masterhood as part of the Sith Grand Plan.]]
The mysterious<ref name="Acolyte Companion">{{InsiderCite|229|Star Wars: The Acolyte Companion|''Star Wars: The Acolyte'' Companion}}</ref> [[Darth]] Plagueis was a legendary<ref name="Skywalker: A Family at War">''[[Skywalker: A Family at War]]''</ref> [[Muun]]<ref name="The Acolyte" /> [[Dark Lord of the Sith]]<ref name="ROTS" /> trained by the [[Sith Master]] [[Darth Tenebrous]].<ref name="BMF" /> At some point during his life, Plagueis acquired the [[protocol droid]] [[11-4D]].<ref name="Tarkin">[[Tarkin (novel)|''Tarkin'']]</ref> During his time as a [[Sith Lord]] and studying the Force, Plagueis acquired a vast amount of knowledge about the dark side and its teachings.<ref name="ROTS" />

During the [[High Republic Era]], Plagueis was actively working against the [[Jedi]].<ref name="PlagueisDB" /> By [[132 BBY]],<ref name="AcolyteDate">{{TheAcolyteDate}}</ref> he had taken on<ref name="Leslye EW" /> a former [[Jedi]]—a [[human]]<ref name="The Acolyte" /> known as "[[the Stranger]]" or by the pseudonym "Qimir"<ref name="Qimir Databank">{{Databank|qimir|The Stranger (alias "Qimir")}}</ref>—as his apprentice.<ref name="Leslye EW" /> In that [[Standard year|year]],<ref name="AcolyteDate" /> Plagueis was present on an [[The Stranger's island|island]] on<ref name="The Acolyte" /> the [[planet]]<ref name="AcolyteVG">''[[Star Wars: The Acolyte: The Visual Guide]]''</ref> [[Bal'demnic]],<ref name="Fry">{{EmailCite|email=File:AtlasEmail-2025-10-24.png|creator=[[Jason Fry]]|date=2025-10-24}}</ref> which was inhabited by the Stranger. While there, he lurked in the shadows of [[the Stranger's cave]] abode as he observed the Stranger and the former Jedi [[Padawan]] [[Verosha Aniseya]], whom the Stranger would take on as a [[Sith acolyte]], depart from the planet in their [[Starship|ship]], ''[[Exile II]]''.<ref name="The Acolyte" /> Plagueis was still lurking there when the Stranger and Aniseya returned,<ref name="Acolyte Companion" /> with Aniseya by that time having chosen to become the Stranger's acolyte.<ref name="The Acolyte" /> Plagueis's lurking—combined with the Stranger's preference to consider himself someone without a name, rather than directly calling himself a Sith—called into question the Stranger's ties to the Sith and loyalty to Plagueis.<ref name="229POV">{{InsiderCite|229|A Certain Point of View (department)}}</ref>

===Master of Darth Sidious===
{{Quote|My mentor taught me everything about the Force, even the nature of the dark side.|Sheev Palpatine|<ref name="ROTS" />}}
[[File:Rise-of-Palpatine.png|thumb|left|220px|Darth Sidious was the secret persona of Sheev Palpatine and the Sith apprentice of Darth Plagueis.]]
The precise [[time]] when Plagueis came to acquire his new [[Sith apprentice]] was unknown,<ref name="Star Wars Book">''[[The Star Wars Book]]''</ref> but the Dark [[Lord]] chose [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]], a [[human]] from [[Naboo]], as his pupil. As master and disciple, Plagueis and Palpatine—who took the Sith moniker Darth Sidious—worked together for [[Standard year|years]], trying to unlock the secrets of [[immortality]] as Plagueis lusted for it<ref name="Tarkin" /> and to execute the [[Sith]] Order's [[Grand Plan|long-percolating plan]] of supplanting the [[Galactic Republic]] with a new [[Sith Empire]].<ref name="SWEsid">{{SWE|characters|darthsidious|Darth Sidious}}</ref>

While training Sidious, Plagueis taught him that two Sith were required for their perilous machinations. So, if they worked together in accordance to the [[Rule of Two]], with one of them serving as a bait for the [[dark side of the Force]] and the other as a vessel, they would succeed in acquiring the ability to harness the full power of the dark side and rule immortal for ten thousand years.<ref name="Tarkin" /> While apprenticed by Plagueis, Sidious also built his [[Darth Sidious' lightsabers|own]] [[lightsaber]]s.<ref name="USW">''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]''</ref>

Believing the secrets to immortality to lie in science, Plagueis conducted in-depth research into the biological underpinnings of life. Some of that research constituted unnatural experiments, through his ability to coax the [[midi-chlorian]]s, in an attempt to cheat death, that, though incomplete, were encouraging to his apprentice.<ref name="Star Wars Book" /> The Sith Order had long coveted the ability to live forever, unwilling to accept the [[Jedi Order]]'s belief that death was a natural part of life, but over the [[Standard century|centuries]] generations of [[Sith Lord]]s failed to unlock the ability that led to eternal life.<ref name="Secrets of the Sith">''[[Star Wars: The Secrets of the Sith]]''</ref> He was so obsessed with the subject that he ignored the signs that his "faithful apprentice" was progressing in a disturbing way for him.<ref name="Palpatine">{{EncyclopediaCite|Emperor Palpatine}}</ref>

[[File:Dyad.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Inspired by the Doctrine of the Dyad, Plagueis tried to facilitate a powerful bond with Sidious.]]
According to Darth Sidious' [[book]], ''[[The Secrets of the Sith]]'', Plagueis discovered a form of immortality through [[transference]], a [[Force power]] that allowed the user to transfer his consciousness to another body, essentially using bodies as vessels.<ref name="Secrets of the Sith" /> Plagueis also attempted to forge a [[Force dyad]] with Sidious, a unique [[Force-bond]] as strong as life itself, which was discovered from the [[Doctrine of the Dyad]], the [[Doctrine of the Dyad|predecessor]] to the Rule of Two. However, Plagueis was unsuccessful in forming the dyad.<ref name="IX Novel">''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: Expanded Edition]]''</ref>

Darth Plagueis had arranged for his apprentice to become the [[Senator]] of Naboo and the rest of the [[Chommell sector]]<ref name="Palpatine" /> with Palpatine being elected in [[52 BBY]].<ref name="Star Wars: Timelines">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]''</ref> By the time that Sidious, under his public persona of Sheev Palpatine, was appointed to the [[Galactic Senate]] as the Senator of Naboo, Plagueis was still teaching him,<ref name="Tarkin" /> which allowed Palpatine to sharpen his political skills within the plan imagined for him by his master, before they returned to [[Coruscant]].<ref name="Palpatine" />

===The death of Darth Plagueis===
{{Quote|Unfortunately, he taught his apprentice everything he knew. Then his apprentice killed him in his sleep.|Sheev Palpatine|<ref name="ROTS" />}}
According to Sidious, Plagueis was powerful enough that he could use [[the Force]] to influence the midi-chlorians to create life and keep the ones he cared about from [[Death|dying]], a precious knowledge that awarded him the epithet of "the Wise."<ref name="explEPIII" /> However, Plagueis also developed a belief that the Force could "strike back" at him for his power.<ref name="Tarkin" /> In truth, he became so powerful that the only thing he still dreaded was losing his power.<ref name="ROTS" />

[[File:Sith_Lords_Trade_Federation.png|thumb|left|300px|Under the Rule of Two, Sidious killed his master and trained his own Sith apprentice, Darth Maul.]]
Ultimately, Plagueis' only fear was bound to come true; at some point, Sidious had learned everything he needed from his<ref name="ROTS" /> distracted master,<ref name="Palpatine" /> after which he decided that he had no further use for his teacher. In accordance with the Rule of Two tradition,<ref name="Star Wars Book" /> Sidious broke into his master's [[Darth Plagueis' apartment|apartment]]<ref name="Palpatine" /> and disposed of Plagueis, murdering his mentor in cold blood, killing him in his [[sleep]],<ref name="ROTS" /> and ascending to ultimate power and acquiring the title of Sith Master for himself.<ref name="Star Wars Book" /> As noted by Sidious, Plagueis did not act fast enough to prevent his own demise.<ref name="IX Novel" /> Sometime before or after Plagueis' demise, Sidious acquired his own pupil in the [[Nightsisters|Nightsister]] [[Mother (title)|Mother]] [[Talzin]]'s son, [[Maul|Darth Maul]],<ref name="explEPIII" /> a young [[Dathomirian]] [[Zabrak]] whom Sidious had accepted from Talzin when he was only a [[Youngling|child]].<ref name="SonOfDathomir3">[[Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir 3|''Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir'' 3]]</ref>

===Legacy===
====The rise of Darth Sidious====
{{Quote|But darkness is eternal. Unlike the light, it cannot be extinguished. It will always find a way to rise again. And I, Darth Sidious, have risen with it.|Darth Sidious|<ref name="Secrets of the Sith" />}}
[[File:Sidious_Son_of_Dathomir.png|thumb|right|250px|Plagueis' legacy was inherited by Sidious, who used his mentor's knowledge to further his own ambitions.]]
Sidious accomplished his ascendance as a Dark Lord of the Sith by killing Plagueis, adhering to the Sith Order's tradition in which the apprentice completed his dark-side training by killing his master.<ref name="Secrets of the Sith" /> Plagueis' legacy continued through Sidious; With the death of Plagueis, Sidious not only gained the status of Master, but also acquired 11-4D, the late Sith Lord's multi-[[limb]]ed [[Aide|assistant]].<ref name="Tarkin" /> In addition, Sidious also inherited Plagueis' studies; in depth research into the biological underpinnings of life with the end goal of discovering how to cheat death.<ref name="Star Wars Book" />

Plagueis' death served as an example to the apprentice who betrayed and killed him; Sidious regarded his master's trust in him as a mistake, which he vowed to never make. During the [[Clone Wars]], Sidious was aware that his second apprentice, [[Dooku|Darth Tyranus]], plotted to usurp his title of Sith Master by killing him. Sensing that Tyranus' betrayal was imminent, Sidious successfully conspired to have his student killed by his intended replacement, the [[Jedi Knight]] and prophesied [[Chosen One]] [[Anakin Skywalker]].<ref name="Secrets of the Sith" />

====The Tragedy of Darth Plagueis the Wise====
{{Quote|Did you ever hear the Tragedy of Darth Plagueis the Wise?|Sheev Palpatine, to Anakin Skywalker|<ref name="ROTS" />}}
[[File:Palpatine_and_Anakin.png|thumb|left|300px|Anakin Skywalker learned about the late Darth Plagueis as recounted by Sheev Palpatine.]]
In the waning [[Standard day|days]] of the Republic, Sidious recounted the [[Timeline of galactic history|history]] of his late master to Skywalker, whom he befriended years before the [[Cloning|Clone]] Wars in an effort to gradually turn him to the dark side of the Force. Skywalker, who was unaware at the time that his friend was in fact a Sith Lord, and having developed premonitions of his [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|secret wife's]] death in [[Reproduction|childbirth]], was intrigued by the story of Plagueis, particularly his ability to prevent death. When the fear of loss drove Skywalker to betray the Jedi Order, turning him into the Sith Lord Darth Vader, Sidious [[Proclamation of the New Order|reformed]] the Republic into the [[Galactic Empire]] and declared himself [[Galactic Emperor|Emperor]]. At the same time, he had the Jedi [[Great Jedi Purge|systematically executed]] throughout [[the galaxy]] by [[Order 66]], completing the Sith plan that lasted for over a [[millennium]].<ref name="ROTS" />

One of the few Jedi to survive was a [[Padawan]] named [[Ferren Barr]]. Barr began investigating as to why the Jedi fell so quickly and learned of Plagueis' existence, putting his file on him in his list of individuals involved in the crisis.<ref name="Dark Lord 14">[[Darth Vader (2017) 14|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 14]]</ref> In the years that followed his rise to power, Sidious came to genuinely, if posthumously, appreciate Plagueis for the planner and [[prophet]] he had been. Sometimes, Sidious mused about how his late master would have reacted when confronted with the trivial, day-to-day matters of Imperial [[politics]], remarking that Plagueis never foresaw that he would become [[Emperor]]. Sidious desired not just the immortaltiy his master had craved<ref name="Tarkin" /> and achieved,<ref name="Secrets of the Sith" /> but the power to [[Alter Reality|fashion a universe of his own creation]], and make it so the Force could not "strike back".<ref name="Tarkin" />

[[File:SidEmp.png|thumb|right|300px|Plagueis' apprentice ultimately became the Emperor of the First Galactic Empire.]]
Plagueis' failure to form a dyad with his apprentice had convinced Sidious that his master was unworthy of the task. However, Sidious also failed to recreate the dyad with his own disciple Vader, despite their combined power as scions of the two strongest Force-sensitive [[blood]]lines, the [[Palpatine family|Palpatines]] and the [[Skywalker family|Skywalkers]].<ref name="Secrets of the Sith" /> In [[3 ABY]],<ref name="SotS Date">The flashback in which Darth Plagueis is mentioned in ''[[Shadow of the Sith]]'' takes place place concurrently with [[Darth Vader (2020) 11|''Darth Vader'' (2020) 11]], which ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of to [[3 ABY]].</ref> cultists searching the catacombs beneath the [[Sith Citadel]] on the planet [[Exegol]], a secret Sith world that Palpatine had taken over, repeated Plagueis' name in something similar to a chant, along with the names of other Sith.<ref name="SotS">''[[Shadow of the Sith]]''</ref>

====Transference====
{{Quote|For centuries, our Order has seen the dark side of the Force as a means of achieving immortality. Yet none were able to unlock that secret…until Darth Plagueis the Wise. My master discovered ways to use the Force to keep others from perishing. But, alas, for all his infinite wisdom, he still could not save himself from death at the hand of his trusted apprentice.|Darth Sidious|<ref name="Secrets of the Sith" />}}
[[File:First_Death_2.png|thumb|left|250px|Sidious used Plagueis' methods to transfer his consciousness to a new body after his first demise.]]
During the [[Battle of Endor]] in [[4 ABY]],<ref name="Galactic Atlas">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]''</ref> Sidious was killed by a redeemed Anakin Skywalker, who turned back to the [[light side of the Force]] and threw Sidious down a reactor shaft to save his son [[Luke Skywalker]].<ref name="ROTJ">{{Film|VI}}</ref> While falling, however, Sidious reflected that he had prepared himself for that scenario unlike Plagueis and called on all the power of the dark side to leave his body and thrust his consciousness to a cloned body created by the [[Sith Eternal]] on the secret Sith world of Exegol.<ref name="IX Novel" />

When Sidious used Plagueis' secret to immortality<ref name="IX Novel" /> and his own research into mix of [[Sith sorcery]] and technology<ref name="Palpatine" /> to resurrect his spirit in a new vessel,<ref name="Secrets of the Sith" /> he was able to stave off death for a time, but immortality still eluded the Dark Lord. To this end, the transfer was imperfect;<ref name="Star Wars Book" /> when Sidious thrusted his essence toward the new cloned vessel, and had awoken, he realized the painful, temporary existence he was now within, the body racked with decay in consequence to his massive power within the dark side of the Force, leading the Sith Lord toward death permanently if not dealt with. Because of this, Sidious mused that perhaps Plagueis, in the end, was having the final laugh over his apprentice, as karma for his demise.<ref name="IX Novel" />

[[File:PalpatineExegol-TROS.png|thumb|right|270px|Sidious managed to cheat death by transfering his soul to the clone body using Plagueis' techniques.]]
In the years following the Empire's [[Battle of Jakku|end]], during the final stages of the [[First Order-Resistance War|war]] between the [[First Order]] and the [[Resistance]], Sidious' granddaughter, [[Rey Skywalker|Rey]] tracked him down to Exegol as the Resistance and the Sith Eternal prepared for a [[Battle of Exegol|final showdown]].<ref name="Episode IX">{{Film|IX}}</ref> Before a redeemed [[Ben Solo]] came to her rescue, Sidious insisted his granddaughter to strike him down as he did with Plagueis, allowing Rey to read his mind and discover how he came back thanks to Plagueis' teachings. Ultimately, Rey used the voices and power of the past and deceased Jedi to permanently destroy Sidious and the Sith for good.<ref name="IX Novel" />

In the wake of victory at the aftermath of the Battle of Exegol, the [[Exegol Excavation Project]] was launched to excavate the Sith Citadel on Exegol. The archeological endeavor led by [[Beaumont Kin]] managed to uncover a file regarding Darth Plagueis within the [[Arcane Library]]. According to Kin's notes as provided in the book ''[[The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire]]'', the file was notably defaced, but the information contained within brought to life the existence of Darth Plagueis and help construct an incomplete hierarchy of information about the known Sith Lords.<ref name="Rise">''[[Star Wars: The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire]]''</ref>

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|He became so powerful, the only thing he was afraid of was…losing his power, which eventually of course he did.|Sheev Palpatine, to Anakin Skywalker|<ref name="ROTS" />}}
[[File:SecretsoftheSith-Darth-Plagueis.png|thumb|left|250px|Darth Plagueis (silhouette pictured) was a wise Sith Lord who became paranoid as he grew in power.]]
Darth Plagueis was a Dark Lord of the Sith who possessed a vast knowledge of the dark side of the Force.<ref name="explEPIII" /> He was a [[Muun]]<ref name="PlagueisDB" /> and had [[Color|yellow]] and red [[eye]]s.<ref name="The Acolyte" /> He was a meticulous planner, who tried to accomplish the Sith's goal to replace the Galactic Republic with a Sith Empire. Due to his powers, he also became paranoid, believing that the Force could "strike back."<ref name="Tarkin" />

Obsessed with achieving immortality, Plagueis strived to discover the path towards becoming an eternal being alongside his apprentice Darth Sidious and rule together for thousands of years,<ref name="Tarkin" /> and believed the secret to it laid in science. His desire to cheat death represented a subversion of the natural order of things and an ultimate act of manipulation of the universe and the will of the Force.<ref name="Star Wars Book" /> While Plagueis became afraid of losing his power, he never expected his apprentice to be the reason he would lose power. Ultimately, Plagueis had trusted<ref name="Secrets of the Sith" /> and underestimated Sidious, who betrayed and murdered him when he least expected it. Though Plagueis did not live to achieve his goals, Sidious succeeded to survive his own death, but given that his transfer was imperfect, he asked himself if maybe Plagueis got the last laugh after all at his failure.<ref name="IX Novel" />

==Powers and abilities==
{{Quote|Ironic. He could save others from death, but not himself.''"<br />"''Is it possible to learn this power?''"<br />"''Not from a Jedi.|Sheev Palpatine and Anakin Skywalker|<ref name="ROTS" />}}
[[File:Tragedy.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Sidious remembered Plagueis as a powerful Sith who discovered the ability to achieve immortality.]]
According to Darth Sidious, Darth Plagueis was a powerful Sith Lord who was able to use the Force to influence the midi-chlorians to create life,<ref name="ROTS" /> a power that was reportedly to be extremely rare for one sensitive to the Force to possess, and could even be used by certain Sith Lords to prolong their life or even cheat death. Utilizing this ability, Plagueis was able to conduct unnatural experimentations in his bid to discover immortality.<ref name="Star Wars Book" /> His great knowledge of the dark side of the Force could also even aid him in keeping the ones he cared about from dying.<ref name="ROTS" />

Focused on achieving immortality through sciences and the biologicial underpinnings of life,<ref name="Star Wars Book" /> Darth Plagueis managed to discover a way to become immortal, which consisted on transferring his consciousness to another body and use it like a vessel. Plagueis did not have time, however, to use this skill to evade death when his student cut him down. His apprentice Darth Sidious was later able to survive his first death through this method, yet the transfer was imperfect.<ref name="IX Novel" />

Darth Plagueis may have had the ability to see into the future as his apprentice later mused in appreciation of him for the prophet he had been. However, what Plagueis never saw coming was his apprentice's rise to power.<ref name="Tarkin" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Origins and development===
[[File:ThatsNoMuun.png|thumb|left|250px|Darth Plagueis made his first "appearance" in canon through a silhouette in the reference book ''Star Wars Made Easy''.]]
Darth Plagueis was first mentioned on-screen in the [[2005]] film [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']], the third and final installment of the ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[prequel trilogy]].<ref name="ROTS" /> Although Palpatine was never confirmed to be Plagueis' apprentice in the movie itself, a link to the [[Encyclopedia (StarWars.com)|official encyclopedia]] on [[StarWars.com]] did refer to Sidious as having been "trained by Darth Plagueis."<ref name="explEPIII" /> He first appeared unnamed in "[[The Acolyte (episode)|The Acolyte]]," the eponymous eighth episode of the [[2024]] television series ''[[Star Wars: The Acolyte]]'',<ref name="The Acolyte" /> his identity in the episode being later confirmed by showrunner [[Leslye Headland]] in an interview.<ref name="confirmation">{{WebCite|url=https://www.indiewire.com/features/interviews/the-acolyte-finale-darth-plagueis-reveal-confirmed-leslye-headland-1235026659|text='The Acolyte' Finale Is a Plagueis on Both Their Houses, Leslye Headland Tells Us|author=Sarah Shachat|work=[[Wikipedia:IndieWire|IndieWire]]|date=2024-07-17|archivedate=20240717221050}}</ref> There, the character's appearance in the episode was rendered entirely with [[Wikipedia:Computer-generated imagery|computer-generated imagery]], without the use of [[Wikipedia:Motion picture|motion capture]].<ref name="Headland Collider interview">{{WebCite|url=https://collider.com/the-acolyte-episode-8-explained-leslye-headland|text=Leslye Headland Confirms That Major 'Acolyte' Finale Cameo: "Yeah, Baby. Plagueis."|author=Maggie Lovitt|date=2024-07-18|work=[[Wikipedia:Collider (website)|Collider]]|archivedate=20240808082415}}</ref> Before his appearance in ''The Acolyte'',<ref name="The Acolyte" /> Plagueis was first pictured via silhouette in the reference book ''[[Star Wars Made Easy]]''.<ref name="SWEasy">''[[Star Wars Made Easy]]''</ref>

The character was created by [[George Lucas]] as early as the first draft of ''Revenge of the Sith''—dated [[April]] [[2003]]—and possibly earlier.<ref name="The Making of Star Wars Revenge of the Sith">''[[The Making of Star Wars Revenge of the Sith]]''</ref> His story was massively expanded upon in the [[2012]] [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] novel [[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']], written by [[James Luceno]].<ref name="Plagueis">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref> It notably established [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Plagueis]] to be a [[Muun/Legends|Muun]], just as Lucas proposed,<ref name="TheForce.net 2012 Luceno interview">{{WebCite|url=http://theforce.net/latestnews/story/Interview_Plagueis_Author_James_Luceno_142844.asp|text=Interview: Plagueis Author James Luceno|author=Eric Geller|date=2012-01-10|work=[[TheForce.net]]|archivedate=20160506025257}}</ref> a trait that was used once more in ''The Acolyte''<ref name="The Acolyte" /> and had been canonized prior by the reference book ''[[Endless Vigil]]''.<ref name="Endless">''[[Endless Vigil]]''</ref> All the same, prior to ''The Acolyte'',<ref name="The Acolyte" /> Plagueis' canon appearance was kept hidden via his silhouettes in ''Star Wars Made Easy''<ref name="SWEasy" /> and ''[[Star Wars: The Secrets of the Sith]]''.<ref name="Secrets of the Sith" /> Plagueis was always intended to appear in the season 1 finale of ''The Acolyte''.<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://sffgazette.com/sci_fi/star-wars/the-acolyte-showrunner-explains-spoilers-expanded-universe-cameo-and-what-it-means-for-the-future-a8275|text=THE ACOLYTE Showrunner Explains SPOILER's Expanded Universe Cameo And What It Means For The Future|author=Josh Wilding|date=2024-07-18|work=SFF Gazette|archivedate=20240726021350}}</ref> Headland later confirmed that Plagueis was the Master of "the Stranger" when speaking with [[Entertainment Weekly Books|''Entertainment Weekly'']]. Having been talking immediately beforehand about the character's cameo in the episode alongside that of [[Yoda]], Headland stated "We wanted to show Qimir's master. We weren't going to wait a second season for that."<ref name="Leslye EW" />

===Canon details===
[[File:PlagueisNSSGF.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Darth Plagueis, as depicted in ''Star Wars'' Legends]]
Although Legends works show that Plagueis had power over life and death, Lucas himself stated Palpatine's tale about Plagueis' abilities was a lie.<ref name="SW Archives">''[[The Star Wars Archives: Episodes I–III, 1999–2005]]''</ref> Canon also dispensed with the idea of these powers being a lie.<ref name="IX Novel" /> The Biography gallery of Darth Sidious' [[Databank (2014-)|Databank]] entry<ref name="explEPIII" /> and the "Senator Palpatine" card part of [[2020 Topps Star Wars Holocron Series|2020 Topps ''Star Wars'' Holocron Series]]<ref name="2020Holocron">{{Topps|set=2020 Topps Star Wars Holocron Series|cardname=Senator Palpatine|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/231065/cid/15795297/2020-Topps-Star-Wars-Holocron-Series-Rep-3-Senator-Palpatine}}</ref> both state that Plagueis was killed by Sidious after he took Darth Maul as his apprentice. However, the [[2019]] reference book ''[[Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition]]'' lists Plagueis' murder at Sidious' hands as taking place before Sidious takes Maul under his wing.<ref name="USW,NE">''[[Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition]]''</ref>

Luceno's Legends novel also established Plagueis's public identity of Hego Damask, head of the clandestine financial group [[Damask Holdings/Legends|Damask Holdings]].<ref name="Plagueis" /> The [[2015]] canon reference book ''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]'' went onto feature a mention of Damask, taking<ref name="USW">''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]''</ref> an exchange about the [[Naboo (people)/Legends|Naboo]] [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Theed/Legends|Theed]] between "Damask" and a young [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] from before he became the Muun's [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]].<ref name="Plagueis" /> However, [[Pablo Hidalgo]] of the [[Lucasfilm Story Group]] later confirmed this mention of Damask was not meant to be featured in the finalized book.<ref name="Pablo Hidalgo Tweet">{{Twitter|pablohidalgo|status/678278140599271424|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|quote=Add that to Lothal TIE fighters, B-wing history and a Hego Demask reference that shouldn't be in there...|nobackup=1}}</ref> Nonetheless, [[Damask Holdings]] itself has since been confirmed to exist within canon,<ref name="Star Wars: Timelines" /> but no source at this time has linked the company to Plagueis in canon.

=== LEGO media ===
In the [[2025]] limited [[Disney+]] series ''[[LEGO Star Wars: Rebuild the Galaxy - Pieces of the Past]]'s'' [[Part Four (Pieces of the Past)|fourth episode]], Darth Plagueis is mentioned by Jedi Palpatine when [[Sig Greebling]] gives a speech, saying Sig talked more than Darth Plagueis "the Long-Winded."<ref name="Part Four">{{PiecesOfThePast|Part Four}}</ref>
